text:
maria: Quick note, onboarding protoflux-9b (llama->mistral hybrid export). seeing subtle token dropout around repeated nouns in long context when running int4. not present in fp16.

ken: Can you repro with a short script and attach model metadata?

maria: yep. small repro attached to bench job. metadata: export_mode=llama-compat, head_layout=interleaved, rotary=per-head, kv_layout=qkv, quant=grouped-int4, bucket=64.

convert-bot: conversion complete. checksum: abc123. warnings: head_order_hint missing in header, rotary_scale variations detected.

yusuf: head_order_hint missing could mean exporter used interleaved head packing. our runtime assumes grouped by default. That can shift how sin/cos apply across slices.

leah: low-hanging check: run a headwise kv-compare between fp16 and int4 for the prompt that drops tokens. use L2 norm per head.

maria: ran it. heads 2,5,8 show elevated L2 (~0.02) after token 120. others ~<0.003.

ken: do you see mismatches in projection order? if q,k,v order swapped vs runtime we apply sin/cos to wrong tensors.

maria: projection order seems correct per header (qkv). i dumped first-layer proj matrices and values match elementwise within 1e-4 pre-quant. post-quant they're coarser but not reordered.

yusuf: then maybe rotary phase indexing off-by-offset for interleaved layout. our per-head sin/cos table assumes contiguous head blocks. for interleaved we need stride-aware indexing.

leah: can you try re-export with head_layout=grouped and rerun quant? that'll test whether mapping is the issue.

maria: I kicked off two runs: (A) re-export grouped + int4 bucket=64, (B) keep interleaved but convert rotary=shared. preliminary: A reduced dropout significantly, B helped a bit but not fully.

ken: suggests interleaved + per-head rotary + int4 interaction triggers the bug. likely quant packing changes memory layout and our sin/cos gather is using wrong stride.

convert-bot: perf artifact: https://internal/bench/1761238901/protoflux-int4-sweep (latency 1.9x perf vs fp16, mem 3.5x savings).

yusuf: action plan: 1) add support in runtime for interleaved head indexing when applying rotary (stride arg), 2) add converter normalization step that reorders heads into grouped layout as fallback, 3) extend unit test to compare kv matrices headwise after quantization.

maria: i'm on 2) — implementing a converter reordering pass and a small normalization that rescales sin/cos by per-head weight norm post-quant. opening PR shortly.

leah: i'll take 1) — runtime patch to accept head_stride param in rotary kernel and add a flag to autodetect via header hints. will add microbench to ensure no perf regression.

ken: for tests, include long-context summarization and codegen evals. this dropout affected repetition of named entities, so include entity-heavy prompts.

maria: added those to the eval set and queued regression. linking artifact when ready.

yusuf: one more: check tokenizer sentinel handling — hybrid exporters sometimes fold multi-char sentinels into single ids, changing position alignment in long contexts. verify token sequences are identical across runs.

maria: verified token sequences identical for repro prompts. not the root cause here.

ken: cool. ping when PRs up and we'll run the full eval sweep. thanks everyone. :rocket:
